q: Zimmer's cocycle superrigidity theorem (1980) constrains derivative cocycles of smooth lattice actions. It says measurable cocycles Γ×X→GL(n,ℝ) are:
opts: Cohomologous to algebraic maps (composition of a group homomorphism Γ→GL(n,ℝ) and a measurable map into a compact group)
Determined by the entropy of the action
exp: Zimmer's cocycle superrigidity: for higher-rank lattices, measurable cocycles into GL(n,ℝ) are cohomologous to 'algebraic' ones (coming from representations of the ambient Lie group G). This constrains the derivative of any smooth action — the key step toward the Zimmer conjecture.
